title: Linked List Cycle
statement: A singly linked list is given as an array of values plus an integer pos, where pos is the index that the tail connects back to (-1 means the tail points to null). Return true if the list contains a cycle, otherwise false. A pos of 0 with a non-empty list is a cycle.

examples.explanation: The tail (-4) links back to index 1 (value 2).
The tail points to null, so there is no cycle.

hints: A cycle exists exactly when pos is a valid index (pos >= 0) and the list is non-empty.
The classic proof uses slow (1 step) and fast (2 steps) pointers meeting inside the loop.
Simulate the walk with a visited set to confirm the pointer reasoning.

solutions.title: Visited Index Set
Direct Position Check

editorial.approach: Floyd's Cycle-Finding Algorithm (Tortoise and Hare): initialize two pointers, slow moving one step and fast moving two steps per iteration. If a cycle exists, fast will enter the cycle and eventually lap and collide with slow. If fast or fast.next reaches null, no cycle exists.
editorial.why_optimal: Operates in O(N) time with strict O(1) space, avoiding hash set pointer tracking that consumes linear heap memory.
editorial.pitfalls: Dereferencing fast.next.next without first validating that fast and fast.next are both non-null. Initializing pointers such that slow == fast evaluates to true before the first iteration begins.
